objectClass.notes: Eleven-story naked-eye observatory carved into a mesa edge: V-shaped entry channel with outward-leaning flagstone walls leads to a circular excavated bowl rimmed by a crescent fieldstone wall with two bastion pylons; a 147-step granite stairway (Star Tunnel) rises at the site latitude angle (~34.5 deg) aligned to Polaris, passing a freestanding triangular (A-frame) portal, ending in a stainless-steel cylinder aperture; a ~55 ft sandstone-clad Solar Pyramid with a granite edge-stair sits at the top of the mound beside the bowl; Hour Chamber wedge (15 deg) inside pyramid base; flat Shadow Field terrain beyond.

reasoning: Six macro assemblies visible across references: terrain/mesa, entry channel, crescent bowl wall, star tunnel stair system, solar pyramid, sky/light rig.
Heavy repetition systems: 147 stair treads, flagstone slab cladding, fieldstone rubble courses, ashlar block courses.
Occlusion risk is low because eight reference photos cover entry, interior, apex, night and aerial views.
Materials split into six distinct PBR families with strong roughness/albedo separation (rubble vs ashlar vs brushed steel).

specDepthDecision.rationale: Architectural monument with four repetition systems and six material families; identity depends on precise angular relationships (34.5 deg stair axis, 15 deg hour wedge, solstice-angled pyramid faces), so component-level pivots and named sockets (sun rig, polaris axis, camera stations) are required.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: Exact plan-view footprint dimensions are approximated from '11 stories tall, 1/10 mile across' and photo proportions; stated as approximate.
South/rear elevation of the pyramid mound is inferred from aerial and apex shots; stylization stated.
Interior equatorial chamber geometry simplified to the visible triangular-notch room.

detailInventory.note: Filled from direct inspection of 8 reference photos plus 3x3 grid crops of the primary aerial reference.

details.description: Crescent bowl wall lower band: irregular tan/buff fieldstone rubble, stone sizes 0.2-1.2 m, deep recessed mortar joints, strong per-stone albedo variation (buff, gray, rust).
Upper band of crescent wall: coursed cut-block ashlar, lighter warm gray, topped by a smooth pale granite coping strip that traces the full crescent rim ellipse.
Two truncated sloped-face bastion pylons terminate the crescent wall ends, block masonry, battered faces, flat tops slightly above rim.
147 uniform granite stair treads rise between two smooth granite stringer rails at ~34.5 deg; treads read as light warm gray with crisp nosing shadows.
Dark trapezoid-section tunnel overhang midway up the stair; interior walls lean inward, benches/ledges flank the stair (interior photo).
Top-of-tunnel oculus: brushed stainless-steel cylinder, low roughness anisotropic sheen, framing a perfect sky circle; mounted in a concrete/steel headwall slab above the crescent rim.
Freestanding A-frame (triangular) portal on a masonry terrace at stair base; sandstone block sides, dark interior with visible steps, apex centered on tunnel axis.

Entry channel walls lean outward ~30 deg from vertical, clad in large irregular polygonal sandstone flags (0.5-2 m), colors pink/tan/rust with thin mortar lines; pale concrete coping strip on top edge.
Solar Pyramid faces clad in smooth pink/salmon sandstone slabs with faint rectangular panel seams; face angles set by solstice sun altitudes; thin crisp apex ridge.
Granite stair with parallel stringers climbing the pyramid's north edge to the apex; reads as a zipper of light treads against the salmon face.
Hour Chamber: 29-ft tall, 15-degree wedge aperture; from inside, a knife-thin triangle of sky and desert horizon between two dark converging planes.
Pale packed caliche sand path with scattered gravel drifts; surrounding mesa slopes strewn with rust/tan rock rubble and dry grass tufts; distant flat-topped mesas on horizon.
Night mode: concentric star-trail arcs centered on Polaris low in the north (~34.5 deg altitude), blue-white-amber trail colors, monument in silhouette.

anatomy.note: Architectural object; anatomy track not applicable.

definitionOfDone: The rendered scene matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.
The entry-channel view reads as the site_aerial reference: leaning flagstone walls, crescent rubble wall with coping, centered stair channel, A-frame portal.
The tunnel-interior view up shows a circular brushed-steel aperture framing sky.
Night mode shows concentric star trails centered on Polaris at ~34.5 deg altitude aligned with the tunnel axis.
The pyramid view reads as pyramid_hero: salmon sandstone faces, granite edge stair, curved granite parapet in foreground, high-desert horizon.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Crescent bowl diameter vs tunnel channel width vs portal height match the aerial reference proportions; stair axis inclined at the latitude angle (~34.5 deg) pointing due north.
failureModes: model reads as a generic ziggurat instead of Star Axis
stair angle or crescent curvature guessed wrong

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Six macro assemblies present and correctly placed: terrain, entry channel, crescent bowl, star tunnel system, solar pyramid with hour chamber, sky/sun/star rig.
failureModes: large visible parts merged into one mesh

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Stair run seats into the excavated channel with no floating gaps; portal sits on the terrace platform; steel aperture cylinder embeds into the headwall slab; pyramid edge-stair contacts the face along its full run.

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Six material families with independent albedo/roughness/normal/AO: flagstone cladding, fieldstone rubble, granite ashlar/treads, brushed stainless, cast concrete, desert soil.
Macro (wall bands), meso (stone joints), micro (grain speckle) frequency bands present in TSL procedural materials.
failureModes: one noise texture reused across all channels

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Day mode: low warm sun, physically plausible sky gradient, pyramid casts long triangular shadow onto shadow field.
Night mode: star field rotating about Polaris with optional trail accumulation matching home_bg reference.
Tone mapping and exposure produce the pale-sand / deep-blue-sky value range of the references.

visualDeltaChecks: silhouette and negative-space delta (crescent rim ellipse, A-frame portal triangle, hour wedge)
repetition density and distribution delta (stair treads, flagstone slabs, rubble courses)
material albedo/roughness/normal response delta (salmon sandstone vs buff rubble vs steel)
local feature placement and scale delta (aperture over rim, portal on axis, bastion positions)
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.

authoringInstruction: Assessment filled from direct visual inspection of 8 reference photographs and 3x3 grid crops. Dimensions derived from published facts (11 stories tall, 1/10 mile across, 147 steps, 15-degree hour wedge, ~34.5 deg latitude alignment) and photo proportions; approximations are stated in unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation.
